perspectives.title: AI Models

representative_posts.author: neilturkewitz.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It doesn’t get better than this— a company advertising “REAL AI MODELS.” So don’t get fooled by those artificial AI models. Hold out for the real thing. And have a Coke.

representative_posts.author: surelyyoujokeme.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: AI is not even remotely profitable, and what use it generates seems to mainly come from (guess what) other AI companies who use it for (guess what) designing AI models. What a scam. Jeez. All for a fast monkey at a keyboard with spellcheck and grammar check.

representative_posts.text: I HIGHLY recommend checking this out if you're an artist or people share your commissions or post them on E621. topics.name: AI Harms Art

perspectives.title: AI Harms Art

representative_posts.author: guncelawits.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Still hung up on my conviction that AI is a wildly-contagious thought virus that only infects certain personality types. The uninfected cannot understand what the fuck the infected are on about because, as a virus, there is nothing there beyond the recipe for its own reproduction.

representative_posts.author: alexjquigley.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Will AI be the death of independent study as we know it? In my latest blog, I explore that question. Though some might not agree, I think we'll have to help students work better with AI than always try to prohibit it.

representative_posts.author: socio-steve.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I recognize that whether AI is conscious, whether that has any moral implications, and whether AI has net negative or positive impacts on the economy and society more broadly are all logically distinct, btw. I just think the first question is driving some wild thoughts/fears about the others.

perspectives.brief: AI cannot replicate human creativity.
perspectives.detail:
Artists Reject AI argues that AI cannot replicate human creativity.

The posts defend it in their own words. @walmsley.bsky.social writes, “by freeing humans from the need to create art so that they can more efficiently engage in productive labor, generative AI is the first ontologically Calvinist technology” @kart0ffeldraws.bsky.social writes, “I think my biggest problem with AI is that creativity is such a human thing. We've been doing it in some form or another for as long as we've been a species So off-loading that onto a computer just feels so wrong.” @lordofoverstock.bsky.social writes, “I know this is all woo-woo, but when you create something you put a little piece of your eternal soul in it, and that connects you to every other soul in the universe, and AI cannot replicate that, its an abomination.”

Inside Artists Reject AI, the posts are arguing one position rather than a stack of unrelated claims.

representative_posts.text: RIP Sir Patrick Stewart... The world will be an emptier place without you.

representative_posts.author: humonculuss.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: larrin86.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: For anyone who would like to honor both Patrick Stewart and the season 😱

Other.name: Trick Or Treat

perspectives.title: Few Trick

representative_posts.author: jonathanstegall.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Normally nobody trick or treats on my street, ever, for reasons I don’t understand (although we always took our kid to other neighborhoods with his friends so maybe that’s why). This year we’ve had like five or six groups of kids. Unprecedented.

representative_posts.author: finnanhaddie.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So many families bring their kids to my street for trick-or-treating that the city started closing it to cars a few years ago & it’s great. I no longer have to worry when I see a kid dart across the street because they spotted a friend.

representative_posts.author: plasmaring.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: YEAH I never get trick or treaters even in the city outskirts, I think around here kids mostly either get driven to areas where there are a lot of big houses or they do organized activities

representative_posts.author: alandria.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I got all dressed up and bought candy for #Halloween. Our complex had a lot of trick or treaters. But I was not aware that kids knock on houses but don't go inside stairwell buildings?! We did not get one single kid knocking on our door, and now we have an excessive amount of candy at home. 🙃

representative_posts.author: windowseat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I grew up in a far out suburb (if you could even call it that) and we just kind of wandered around the houses around our house and didn't often run into other kids. I thought since we live less than a block from the school in Minneapolis we'd see trick or treaters but I guess not. 🤷‍♀️

representative_posts.author: cuddlyonmain.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My neighbors used to get grumbly about older kids trick or treating. But we lived next to a rougher area, so the kids would come to our street because it was safe and everyone was nice. The older kids deserve to have fun too.

representative_posts.author: drdarrell-c.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Do you do trick or treat? I think we had 100+ kids

representative_posts.author: lizzy-nyc.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We do this in Manhattan. Trick-or-treating in the building (kids who live in the building, their friends & grandkids of older residents). Then we take the kids to the streets - local businesses and a few blocks that are shut down to traffic and have people sitting on their stoops handing out candy.

representative_posts.author: crayonheart.art
representative_posts.text: as a child, i could walk the nearby 4-6 blocks of houses and be full up for the night....we have lost the whimsy of decorating outdoors and trick or treating for... boo baskets i guess

representative_posts.author: tea-n-me.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We’re in Iowa. We had about 15 (50 in the past years). Most just stood there. No “Trick or Treat” or even “Happy Halloween.” 3 had a joke (it’s been an Iowa thing for years). Very different from past years.

representative_posts.author: martymango0.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: That was something I loved about the town I grew up in. They do a big trick or treat in the historic district around the town green every year. Girl Scouts collected candy for the houses to give out, Boy Scouts sold hot dogs & popcorn & cider night of, & EVERYONE was welcome to go house to house

representative_posts.author: xphoenixrising9.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Who tf is taking their children trick or treating there?!?

representative_posts.author: lvlmleah.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I grew up on Long Island in the 60's. If it was weekend, we all started trick or treating from like 1 or 2 PM. And on school day, got home at 3, changed, and hit the road. I took my nephews out in the 80's in Texas and no one was out until like 7 PM. I was surprised. And it's same in PNW.

representative_posts.author: gearoidmm.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It’s 70 kids over 20 years. On a night that millions of kids are outside. I just came back from trick or treating and there were hordes of kids out on the streets in the dark. It just isn’t a big risk no matter how you want to stretch it. It is a tiny risk being exaggerated by graphs like this

I used to be “that guy” that was stingy with them, but a friend reminded me that for some of them this is their only candy of the year.

representative_posts.author: jillbles.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: chutry.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: jaygeh.bsky.social

representative_posts.text: kids never come here so i don't always buy candy and then i am sad because i do not get to eat the candy that no kids came to collect

representative_posts.author: codyscamp.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yesterday I helped bag candy for an elderly neighbor who gave them to a local church to hand out to the neighborhood children. representative_posts.author: caff.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: nocaltex.bsky.social

The posts defend it in their own words. @dubs0203.bsky.social writes, “Like I’m such a scent person. I need to know exactly what you smell like. Your hair, skin, all of it 🫠” @jeannedsnark.bsky.social writes, “Scent is so important tho” @guauleggyroarks.bsky.social writes, “I am really starting come around to the idea of scent. it tickles my brain in both bad and good ways. I don't like the way other people smell, but I do like the way I smell. But I like the idea of someone's scent feeling like home to me <3”

Inside Scent Importance, the posts are arguing one position rather than a stack of unrelated claims.
